course.learn: Data classification assigns labels based on sensitivity, value, and handling requirements so controls can match the risk. Common organizational labels include public, internal, confidential, and restricted.
course.why: Without classification, organizations either overprotect everything or fail to protect the data that matters most.
course.example: Customer tax records are labeled restricted, requiring encryption, limited access, logging, and approved disposal.
course.exam: Classification drives handling. The exact label names vary by organization; focus on increasing sensitivity and required controls.

course.learn: This section focuses on **Security Measures** within **Data classifications**. Security measures are the controls used to protect the specific data or system being discussed. Common measures include encryption, access control, secure storage, monitoring, legal/compliance controls, and integrity protection.
course.why: Different data types require different handling based on sensitivity, business value, and legal obligations.
course.example: Sensitive legal records are encrypted, restricted to authorized staff, stored in approved systems, and retained according to policy.
course.exam: Start with the required security objective, then choose controls that directly protect it.
